verses.zh: 所罗门为自己建造宫室，十三年方才造成；
verses.en: Solomon took 13 years to build his palace.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “His house Solomon built in 13 years and he completed all his house.”
verses.commentary:
7:1-8 For Solomon's building projects see Contextual Insights.

7:1 "cubits" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CUBIT.

verses.zh: 又建造黎巴嫩林宫，长一百肘，宽五十肘，高三十肘，有香柏木柱三（原文是四）行，柱上有香柏木柁梁。
verses.en: He named[NOTE:1] it “The Palace of the Lebanon Forest”;[NOTE:2] it was 150 feet[NOTE:3] long, 75 feet[NOTE:4] wide, and 45 feet[NOTE:5] high. It had four rows of cedar pillars and cedar beams above the pillars.
notes: Heb “he built.”

The Palace of the Lebanon Forest. This name was appropriate because of the large amount of cedar, undoubtedly brought from Lebanon, used in its construction. The cedar pillars in the palace must have given it the appearance of a forest.
Heb “100 cubits.”
Heb “50 cubits.”
Heb “30 cubits.”
verses.commentary:
7:2

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, Peshitta
"cedar beams"

REB
"lengths of cedars"

JPSOA
"hewn cedar beams"

Apparently there were cedar pillars and on top of them were cedar beams. The term "hewn beams"
(KB 501) occurs only in 1 Kgs. 6:30; 7:2,12.

verses.zh: 其上以香柏木为盖，每行柱子十五根，共有四十五根。
verses.en: The roof above the beams supported by the pillars was also made of cedar; there were 45 beams, 15 per row.

verses.zh: 有窗户三层，窗与窗相对。
verses.en: There were three rows of windows arranged in sets of three.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and framed [windows in] three rows, and opening to opening three times.” The precise meaning of this description is uncertain. Another option might be, “overhung [in] three rows.” This might mean they were positioned high on the walls.
verses.commentary:
7:4-5 Apparently there were three framed windows on each side, matching the three on the opposite side (see
NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 66, #3,e).

verses.zh: 所有的门框都是厚木见方的，有窗户三层，窗与窗相对。
verses.en: All the entrances[NOTE:1] were rectangular in shape[NOTE:2] and they were arranged in sets of three.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “all of the doors and doorposts.”
Rectangular in shape. That is, rather than arched.
Heb “and all the entrances and the doorposts [had] four frames, and in front of opening to opening three times” (the precise meaning of the description is uncertain).
verses.commentary:
7:5

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA
"doorposts"

TEV, NJB, REB, LXX
"windows"

Peshitta
"posts"

The MT has "doorposts" (BDB 265) but the LXX has "windows."

- and the door posts ‒ והמזוזוח

- and the windows ‒ והמחזות

The UBS Text Project, p. 302, gives the MT a "B" rating (some doubt).

verses.zh: 并建造有柱子的廊子，长五十肘，宽三十肘；在这廊前又有廊子，廊外有柱子和台阶。
verses.en: He made a colonnade[NOTE:1] 75 feet[NOTE:2] long and 45 feet[NOTE:3] wide. There was a porch in front of this and pillars and a roof in front of the porch.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “a porch of pillars.”
Heb “50 cubits.”
Heb “30 cubits.”

Heb “and a porch was in front of them (i.e., the aforementioned pillars) and pillars and a roof in front of them (i.e., the aforementioned pillars and porch).” The precise meaning of the term translated “roof” is uncertain; it occurs only here and in Ezek 41:25-26.
verses.commentary:
7:6

"porch"

NKJV, JPSOA
"portico"

"a covered porch"

"cornice"

"canopy"

Peshitta
"court"

This term (BDB 712 I) is uncertain in meaning. Many translations combine the term above with this
one for "a projecting roof" or some type of wood covering. This is one of many uncertain architectural terms.

verses.zh: 又建造一廊，其中设立审判的座位，这廊从地到顶都用香柏木遮蔽。
verses.en: He also made a throne room, called “The Hall of Judgment,” where he made judicial decisions.[NOTE:1] It was paneled with cedar from the floor to the rafters.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and a porch for the throne, where he was making judicial decisions, the Porch of Judgment, he made.”

The Hebrew text reads, “from the floor to the floor.” The second occurrence of the term הַקַּרְקָע (haqqarqaʿ, “the floor”) is probably an error; one should emend to הַקּוֹרוֹת (haqqorot, “the rafters”). See 6:16.
verses.commentary:
7:7 This verse shows that "the house of the forest of Lebanon" was a separate throne-judgment building.
It was so named because its numerous wooden pillars resembled a forest.

▣

NASB, NRSV, JPSOA
"floor to floor"

NKJV, Peshitta
"floor to ceiling"

TEV, REB, NET
"floor to rafters"

NJB
"floor to beams"

The MT has "floor to floor." The NET Bible suggests an emendation to the second use of "floor" (p. 562).

- the floor ‒ הקרקע (BDB 903)

- the rafter ‒ הקורות

(see 1 Kgs. 6:16; BDEB 885 I, and Ezek. 41:25)

verses.zh: 廊后院内有所罗门住的宫室；工作与这工作相同。所罗门又为所娶法老的女儿建造一宫，做法与这廊子一样。
verses.en: The palace where he lived was constructed in a similar way.[NOTE:1] He also constructed a palace like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had married.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and his house where he lived, the other court [i.e., as opposed to the great court], separated from the house belonging to the hall, was like this work [i.e., this style of architecture].”
Heb “and a house he was making for the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Solomon had taken, like this porch.”
verses.commentary:
7:8 This verse refers to Solomon's palace (cf. 1 Kgs. 7:1).

▣ "a house. . .for Pharaoh's daughter" See Contextual Insights, A. 4.

verses.zh: 建造这一切所用的石头都是宝贵的，是按着尺寸凿成的，是用锯里外锯齐的；从根基直到檐石，从外头直到大院，都是如此。
verses.en: All these were built with the best[NOTE:1] stones, chiseled to the right size[NOTE:2] and cut with a saw on all sides,[NOTE:3] from the foundation to the edge of the roof[NOTE:4] and from the outside to the great courtyard.
notes: Or “valuable” (see 5:17).
Heb “according to the measurement of chiseled [stone].”
Heb “inside and out.”
The precise meaning of the Hebrew word טְפָחוֹת (tefakhot) is uncertain, but it is clear that the referent stands in opposition to the foundation.
verses.commentary:
7:9-12 These verses describe the enclosure that surrounded the complex of royal and sacred buildings. The
symbolism seems to be that the reigning Davidic King was YHWH's representative on earth (i.e., connected to His Temple).

There were two enclosures.

- around the temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:36)

- around the whole building complex (cf. 9:12, royal and sacred)

7:9

"the coping"

NKJV, TEV
"the eaves"

NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 680 (Egyptian plural root)
"roof"

The MT has the term (BDB 381, KB 378) which could mean

- span (cf. Ps. 39:6)

- hand-breadth (cf. 2 Chr. 4:5)

- coping

- KB 378 II suggests "horizontal crossbeam"

- Akkadian, parapet

- see guess by Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, p. 316

The term is obviously in contrast to the foundation, therefore, some structure above.

verses.zh: 根基是宝贵的大石头，有长十肘的，有长八肘的；
verses.en: The foundation was made of large valuable stones, measuring either 15 feet or 12 feet.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “stones of 10 cubits and stones of 8 cubits” (it is unclear exactly what dimension is being measured). If both numbers refer to the length of the stones (cf. NCV, CEV, NLT), then perhaps stones of two different sizes were used in some alternating pattern.

verses.zh: 上面有香柏木和按着尺寸凿成宝贵的石头。
verses.en: Above the foundation[NOTE:1] the best[NOTE:2] stones, chiseled to the right size,[NOTE:3] were used along with cedar.
notes: Heb “on top,” or “above.”
Or “valuable” (see 5:17).
Heb “according to the measurement of chiseled [stone].”

verses.zh: 大院周围有凿成的石头三层、香柏木一层，都照耶和华殿的内院和殿廊的样式。
verses.en: Around the great courtyard were three rows of chiseled stones and one row of cedar beams, like the inner courtyard of the Lord’s temple and the hall of the palace.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “the porch of the temple.”
verses.commentary: 7:12 This verse seems to refer to the house for Pharaoh's daughter.

verses.zh: 所罗门王差遣人往泰尔去，将户兰召了来。
verses.en: King Solomon sent for Hiram[NOTE:1] of Tyre.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “King Solomon sent and took Hiram from Tyre.” In 2 Chr 2:13 (MT v. 12) and 4:11, 16 his name is spelled “Huram.”
For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.
verses.commentary:
7:13 "Hiram from Tyre" This is not Hiram, King of Tyre, but one of the workmen sent from Phoenicia
(cf. 2 Chr. 2:13-14) to Israel. This man was half Israelite and had a special God-given skill (like those who built
the tabernacle, cf. Exod. 28:3; 36:1; 37:1).

The list of all Hiram made is found in 1 Kgs. 7:40-47.

The seeming contradiction between v. 14 and the parallel in 2 Chr. 2:14, where Hiram's mother is
from Dan, can be explained by the fact that in Solomon's day the city of Dan was considered to be in the tribal
allocation of Napthali (see Expositor's Bible Commentary, vol. 4, p. 71).

verses.zh: 他是拿弗他利支派中一个寡妇的儿子，他父亲是泰尔人，作铜匠的。户兰满有智慧、聪明、技能，善于各样铜作。他来到所罗门王那里，做王一切所要做的。
verses.en: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali,[NOTE:1] and his father was a craftsman in bronze from Tyre. He had the skill and knowledge[NOTE:2] to make all kinds of works of bronze. He reported to King Solomon and did all the work he was assigned.
notes: 2 Chr 2:14 (13 HT) says “from the daughters of Dan.”
Heb “he was filled with the skill, understanding, and knowledge.”

verses.zh: 他制造两根铜柱，每根高十八肘，围十二肘；
verses.en: He fashioned two bronze pillars; each pillar was 27 feet[NOTE:1] high and 18 feet[NOTE:2] in circumference.
notes: Heb “18 cubits.”
Heb “12 cubits.”
verses.commentary:
7:15-22 This paragraph describes the two large pillars in front of the temple (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:17; 2 Chr. 3:15-17).

From Jer. 52:21 it seems these tall bronze pillars were hollow.

7:15

verses.zh: 又用铜铸了两个柱顶安在柱上，各高五肘。
verses.en: He made two bronze tops for the pillars; each was 7½ feet high.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “two capitals he made to place on the tops of the pillars, cast in bronze; 5 cubits was the height of the first capital, and 5 cubits was the height of the second capital.”

verses.zh: 柱顶上有装修的网子和拧成的链索，每顶七个。
verses.en: The latticework on the tops of the pillars was adorned with ornamental wreaths and chains; the top of each pillar had seven groupings of ornaments.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “there were seven for the first capital, and seven for the second capital.”

verses.zh: 网子周围有两行石榴遮盖柱顶，两个柱顶都是如此。
verses.en: When he made the pillars, there were two rows of pomegranate-shaped ornaments around the latticework covering the top of each pillar.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he made the pillars, and two rows surrounding one latticework to cover the capitals which were on top of the pomegranates, and so he did for the second latticework.” The translation supplies “pomegranates” after “two rows,” and understands “pillars,” rather than “pomegranates,” to be the correct reading after “on top of.” The latter change finds support from many Hebrew mss and the ancient Greek version.
verses.commentary:
7:18 There is confusion in the translations between "pillars" and "pomegranates."

- pillars ‒ העמודים

- pomegranates ‒ הרמנים

The MT is not clear in this description.

verses.zh: 廊子的柱顶径四肘，刻着百合花。
verses.en: The tops of the two pillars in the porch were shaped like lilies and were six feet high.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the capitals which were on the top of the pillars were the work of lilies, in the porch, 4 cubits.” It is unclear exactly what dimension is being measured.

verses.zh: 两柱顶的鼓肚上挨着网子，各有两行石榴环绕，两行共有二百。
verses.en: On the top of each pillar, right above the bulge beside the latticework, there were 200 pomegranate-shaped ornaments arranged in rows all the way around.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the capitals on the two pillars, also above, close beside the bulge which was beside the latticework, two hundred pomegranates in rows around, on the second capital.” The precise meaning of the word translated “bulge” is uncertain.
verses.commentary:
7:20

NASB, NRSV
"rounded projection"

NKJV
"convex surface"

REB
"all around"

NJB
"raised moulding"

JPSOA
"the bulge"

The MT has the word "belly" (BDB 105) used metaphorically but exactly how is uncertain, as the
translations show.

verses.zh: 他将两根柱子立在殿廊前头：右边立一根，起名叫雅斤；左边立一根，起名叫波阿斯。
verses.en: He set up the pillars on the porch in front of the main hall. He erected one pillar on the right[NOTE:1] side and called it Yakin;[NOTE:2] he erected the other pillar on the left[NOTE:3] side and called it Boaz.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “south.”
The name “Yakin” appears to be a verbal form and probably means, “he establishes.”
Or “north.”

The meaning of the name Boaz is uncertain. For various proposals, see BDB 126-27 s.v. בעז. One attractive option is to revocalize the name as בְּעֹז (beʿoz, “in strength”) and to understand it as completing the verbal form on the first pillar. Taking the words together and reading from right to left, one can translate the sentence, “he establishes [it] in strength.”
verses.commentary:
7:21 "Jachin" This (BDB 467) means "he will establish." The LXX in 2 Chr. 3:17 translates this as "strength."
These two pillars were for decoration, not structural support.

▣ "Boaz" This (BDB 126) could be "in strength," which would match the LXX translation of 2 Chr. 3:17.

Some scholars see the two names being taken together as "YHWH established in strength." Other
temples in this area in this time period have these decorative pillars.

verses.zh: 在柱顶上刻着百合花。这样，造柱子的工就完毕了。
verses.en: The tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. So the construction of the pillars was completed.

verses.zh: 他又铸一个铜海，样式是圆的，高五肘，径十肘，围三十肘。
verses.en: He also made the large bronze basin called “The Sea.”[NOTE:1] It measured 15 feet[NOTE:2] from rim to rim, was circular in shape, and stood 7½ feet[NOTE:3] high. Its circumference was 45 feet.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “He made the sea, cast.”sn This large basin was mounted on twelve bronze bulls and contained water for the priests to bathe themselves (2 Chr 4:6; cf. Exod 30:17-21).
Heb “10 cubits.”
Heb “5 cubits.”

Heb “and a measuring line went around it 30 cubits all around.” The measurements are an approximation. The LXX has the number 33. Neither fit a strict calculation of the diameter time pi, but the precise details of measuring (e.g. the width of the lip or other factors) are not known and numbers may be rounded.
verses.commentary:
7:23-26 This is a description of the water holder for washings of the priests (cf. Exod. 30:20-21; 2 Chr. 4:6).
It took the place of the laver of the tabernacle.

Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 319-320, suggests the large laver was for the priest to
wash and the small portable ones for the washing of sacrifices.

This water container was called by three names.

- the bronze sea ‒ 2 Kgs. 25:13; 1 Chr. 18:8; Jer. 52:17

- the molten sea ‒ 1 Kgs. 7:23; 2 Chr. 4:2

- in Exod. 30:18; 38:8, it is called "a laver of bronze"

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAVER

verses.zh: 在海边之下，周围有野瓜的样式；每肘十瓜，共有两行，是铸海的时候铸上的。
verses.en: Under the rim all the way around it were round ornaments[NOTE:1] arranged in settings 15 feet long.[NOTE:2] The ornaments were in two rows and had been cast with “The Sea.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “gourd-shaped ornaments.”
Heb “10 cubits surrounding the sea all around.” The precise meaning of this description is uncertain.
Heb “the gourd-shaped ornaments were in two rows, cast in its casting.”
verses.commentary: 7:24 "gourds" See 1 Kgs. 6:18 for this same symbolism.

verses.zh: 有十二只铜牛驮海：三只向北，三只向西，三只向南，三只向东；海在牛上，牛尾都向内。
verses.en: “The Sea”[NOTE:1] stood on top of twelve bulls. Three faced northward, three westward, three southward, and three eastward. “The Sea” was placed on top of them, and they all faced outward.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “It.” The proper noun “The Sea” has been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “all their hindquarters were toward the inside.”

verses.zh: 海厚一掌，边如杯边，又如百合花，可容二千罢特。
verses.en: It was four fingers thick and its rim was like that of a cup shaped like a lily blossom. It could hold about 12,000 gallons.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “2,000 baths” (a bath was a liquid measure roughly equivalent to six gallons).
verses.commentary:
7:26 "handbreadth" See #4 in
SPECIAL TOPIC: CUBIT, that shows how the human body was used for measurements.

▣ "baths" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES.

verses.zh: 他用铜制造十个盆座，每座长四肘，宽四肘，高三肘。
verses.en: He also made 10 bronze movable stands. Each stand was 6 feet[NOTE:1] long, 6 feet[NOTE:2] wide, and 4½ feet[NOTE:3] high.
notes: Heb “4 cubits.”
Heb “4 cubits.”
Heb “3 cubits.”

verses.zh: 座的造法是这样：四面都有心子，心子在边子当中，
verses.en: The stands were constructed with frames between the joints.

verses.zh: 心子上有狮子和牛，并基路伯；边上有小座，狮子和牛以下有垂下的璎珞。
verses.en: On these frames and joints were ornamental lions, bulls, and cherubim. Under the lions and bulls were decorative wreaths.[NOTE:1]
notes: The precise meaning of these final words is uncertain. A possible literal translation would be, “wreaths, the work of descent.”
verses.commentary:
7:29 "lions" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS.

▣ "cherubim" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM.

verses.zh: 每盆座有四个铜轮和铜轴。小座的四角上在盆以下，有铸成的盆架，其旁都有璎珞。
verses.en: Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles and four supports.[NOTE:1] Under the basin the supports were fashioned on each side with wreaths.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and four its feet, supports to them.”
The precise meaning of this last word, translated “wreaths,” is uncertain.

verses.zh: 小座高一肘，口是圆的，彷佛座的样式，径一肘半，在口上有雕工，心子是方的，不是圆的。
verses.en: Inside the stand was a round opening that was 18 inches deep; it had a support that was 27 inches long.[NOTE:1] On the edge of the opening were carvings in square frames.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And its opening from the inside to the top and upwards [was] a cubit, and its opening was round, the work of a stand, a cubit-and-a-half.” The precise meaning of this description is uncertain.
Heb “also over its opening were carvings and their frames [were] squared, not round.”

verses.zh: 四个轮子在心子以下，轮轴与座相连，每轮高一肘半。
verses.en: The four wheels were under the frames, and the crossbars of the axles were connected to the stand. Each wheel was 27 inches[NOTE:1] high.
notes: Heb “a cubit-and-a-half” (a cubit was a unit of measure roughly equivalent to 18 inches or 45 cm).

verses.zh: 轮的样式如同车轮；轴、辋、辐、毂都是铸的。
verses.en: The wheels were constructed like chariot wheels; their crossbars, rims, spokes, and hubs were made of cast metal.

verses.zh: 每座四角上都有盆架，是与座一同铸成的。
verses.en: Each stand had four supports, one per side projecting out from the stand.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “four shoulders to the four sides of each stand, from the stand its shoulders.” The precise meaning of the description is uncertain.

verses.zh: 座上有圆架，高半肘；座上有撑子和心子，是与座一同铸的。
verses.en: On top of each stand was a round opening three-quarters of a foot deep;[NOTE:1] there were also supports and frames on top of the stands.
notes: Heb “and on top of the stand, a half cubit [in] height, round all around” (the meaning of this description is uncertain).

verses.zh: 在撑子和心子上刻着基路伯、狮子，和棕树，周围有璎珞。
verses.en: He engraved ornamental cherubim, lions, and palm trees on the plates of the supports and frames wherever there was room,[NOTE:1] with wreaths[NOTE:2] all around.
notes: Heb “according to the space of each.”
The precise meaning of this last word, translated “wreaths,” is uncertain.
verses.commentary:
7:36 "palm trees" This tree (BDB 1071; NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 308-309; UBS Fauna and Flora of the Bible,
pp. 160-162) was sacred in the ANE. It symbolized

- prosperity ‒ Ps. 93:13

- vitality (i.e., evergreen and lived up to 200 years)

- beauty ‒ Song of Songs 7:8

- leadership ‒ Isa. 9:14; 19:15

It decorated

- Solomon's temple

- Ezekiel's temple

- early Jewish coins

verses.zh: 十个盆座都是这样，铸法、尺寸、样式相同。
verses.en: He made the 10 stands in this way. All of them were cast in one mold and were identical in measurements and shape.

verses.zh: 又用铜制造十个盆，每盆可容四十罢特。盆径四肘，在那十座上，每座安设一盆。
verses.en: He also made 10 bronze basins, each of which could hold about 240 gallons.[NOTE:1] Each basin was 6 feet in diameter;[NOTE:2] there was one basin for each stand.
notes: Heb “forty baths” (a bath was a liquid measure roughly equivalent to six gallons).
Heb “4 cubits, each basin.” It is unclear which dimension is being measured.

verses.zh: 五个安在殿门的右边，五个放在殿门的左边；又将海放在殿门的右旁，就是南边。
verses.en: He put five basins on the south side of the temple and five on the north side. He put “The Sea” on the south side, in the southeast corner.

verses.zh: 户兰又造了盆、铲子，和盘子。这样，他为所罗门王做完了耶和华殿的一切工。
verses.en: Hiram also made basins, shovels, and bowls. He[NOTE:1] finished all the work on the Lord’s temple he had been assigned by King Solomon.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Hiram.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “Hiram finished doing all the work which he did for King Solomon [on] the house of the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
7:40

"caldrons"

The MT has a MASCULINE NOUN (BDB 468, KB 492) which has several distinct meanings.

- lavers ‒ Exod. 30:18,28; 31:9; 35:16; 38:8; 39:39; 40:7,11,30; Lev. 8:11; 2 Kgs. 16:17; 2 Chr. 4:6,16

- cooking pot ‒ 1 Sam. 2:14 (also DSS)

- pails ‒ 2 Chr. 4:11,16

- platform of bronze ‒ 2 Chr. 6:13

- firepot ‒ Zech. 12:6

The best guess is #2, used to boil some sacrifices (cf. Lev. 7:15-18).

▣ "bowls" This term (BDB 284) is repeated in 1 Kgs. 7:45. It refers to bronze pots used to remove ashes
from the altar of sacrifice (cf. Exod. 27:3; 38:3; see NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 245).

verses.zh: 所造的就是：两根柱子和柱上两个如球的顶；并两个盖柱顶的网子；
verses.en: He made[NOTE:1] the two pillars, the two bowl-shaped tops of the pillars, the latticework for the bowl-shaped tops of the two pillars,
notes: The words “he made” are added for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 和四百石榴，安在两个网子上，每网两行，盖着两个柱上如球的顶；
verses.en: the 400 pomegranate-shaped ornaments for the latticework of the two pillars (each latticework had two rows of these ornaments at the bowl-shaped top of the pillar),

verses.zh: 十个座和其上的十个盆；
verses.en: the 10 movable stands with their 10 basins,

verses.zh: 海和海下的十二只牛；
verses.en: the big bronze basin called “The Sea” with its 12 bulls underneath,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “underneath ‘The Sea.’”

verses.zh: 盆、铲子、盘子。这一切都是户兰给所罗门王用光亮的铜为耶和华的殿造成的，
verses.en: and the pots, shovels, and bowls. All these items King Solomon assigned Hiram to make for the Lord’s temple[NOTE:1] were made from polished bronze.
notes: Heb “which Hiram made for King Solomon [for] the house of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 是遵王命在约旦平原、疏割和撒拉但中间藉胶泥铸成的。
verses.en: The king had them cast in earth foundries[NOTE:1] in the region of the Jordan between Sukkoth and Zarethan.
notes: Or perhaps, “molds.”

verses.zh: 这一切所罗门都没有过秤；因为甚多，铜的轻重也无法可查。
verses.en: Solomon left all these items unweighed; there were so many of them they did not weigh the bronze.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Solomon left all the items, due to their very great abundance; the weight of the bronze was not sought.”

verses.zh: 所罗门又造耶和华殿里的金坛和陈设饼的金桌子；
verses.en: Solomon also made all these items for the Lord’s temple: the gold altar; the gold table on which was kept the Bread of the Presence;[NOTE:1]
notes: This bread was viewed as a perpetual offering to God and was regarded as holy. See Lev 24:5-9.tn Heb “the bread of the face [or presence].” Many recent English versions employ “the bread of the Presence,” although this does not convey much to the modern reader.
verses.commentary:
7:48-50 A summary of the furnishings of Solomon's temple.

▣ "the golden altar" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ALTAR OF INCENSE.

▣ "the golden table" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SHOW BREAD or BREAD OF THE PRESENCE.

▣ "the lampstand" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LAMPSTAND.

▣ "the inner sanctuary" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF THE WILDERNESS.

Remember, there is symbolism in the metals (gradations of holiness).

- bronze for those things outside the inner shrine

- gold for those things in the inner shrine

verses.zh: 内殿前的精金灯台：右边五个，左边五个，并其上的金花、灯盏、蜡剪，
verses.en: the pure gold lampstands at the entrance to the inner sanctuary (five on the right and five on the left); the gold flower-shaped ornaments, lamps, and tongs;

verses.zh: 与精金的杯、盘、镊子、调羹、火鼎，以及至圣所、内殿的门枢，和外殿的门枢。
verses.en: the pure gold bowls, trimming shears, basins, pans, and censers; and the gold door sockets for the inner sanctuary (the Most Holy Place) and for the doors of the main hall of the temple.

verses.zh: 所罗门王做完了耶和华殿的一切工，就把他父大卫分别为圣的金银和器皿都带来放在耶和华殿的府库里。
verses.en: When King Solomon finished constructing the Lord’s temple, he[NOTE:1] put the holy items that belonged to his father David (the silver, gold, and other articles) in the treasuries of the Lord’s temple.
notes: Heb “Solomon.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Solomon built (ABD, vol. 6, H, pp. 109-110)

- a house for himself ‒ 1 Kgs. 7:1; 9:1,10,15; 10:4

- the house of the Lord ‒ 1 Kings 6; 9:10,15

- the house of the forest of Lebanon (i.e., a public house for judgment where his throne was located, v. 7) ‒
1 Kings 7; 10:17,21

- a house for Pharaoh's daughter ‒ 1 Kgs. 3:1; 7:8; 9:24

- stables for his horses ‒ 1 Kgs. 4:26; 9:19; 10:26

- fortified cities ‒ 1 Kgs. 3:1; 9:15,24

- fleet of ships ‒ 1 Kgs. 9:26; 10:22

- There are many rare architectural terms in 1 Kings 6-7. It is hard to visualize the form of much of Solomon's temple.
He enlarged and elaborated the basic design of the tabernacle. The temple resembled Phoenician temples of the same period.

1Now Solomon was building his own house thirteen years, and he finished all his house.
2He built the house of the forest of Lebanon; its length was 100 cubits and its width 50
cubits and its height 30 cubits, on four rows of cedar pillars with cedar beams on the pillars.
3It was paneled with cedar above the side chambers which were on the 45 pillars, 15 in
each row. 4There were artistic window frames in three rows, and window was opposite
window in three ranks. 5All the doorways and doorposts had squared artistic frames, and
window was opposite window in three ranks.
